text_translated_detailed: Colombo. To the Esteemed Gentlemen Anthony Mooijaert and Marten Rein, Commanders of the commandments of Jaffanapatnam and Candy, as well as the Members of the Secret Committee, Esteemed Commanding Gentlemen of Trincomalee. By letter of the 29th of April, we were informed that the fugitive Kandyan prince was said to be hiding in a forest at Welletje on a mountain and was intending to dispatch envoys to the Coromandel Coast. We could not refrain from fulfilling our duty and have deemed it proper to inform your Esteemed Lordships, under the enclosure of the copy of the aforementioned letter hereto attached, of the required knowledge. With the addition that upon receipt of that letter, we have repeatedly ordered the subordinate posts to maintain a watchful eye both on arriving and departing persons, and thereby also to prevent or intercept all correspondence. With which honor we have, undertaking to name ourselves, Esteemed Commanding Gentlemen, your Esteemed Lordships' obedient and obedient servants, was signed N. A. Lebek, H. Hogerwaerd, J. Herthum, M. van Hek, A. Wierman, J. Panneel, and C. F. Schreu, in the margin Jaffanapatnam the 1st of May, Anno 1765. To the aforementioned. The time having arrived, with the passing of the southwest monsoon, to have the cruising boats stationed at Punto Pedro to Trincomalee along the Wanliasse

By secret resolution of the 2nd of this month, having resolved to employ two of the cruising Pattamars around Manaar, five in number, for the usual yearly cruising east of Punto Pedro to Trincomalee along the Wanliasse shores, on the one hand since the southwest monsoon has long been in progress and thus the best time is to watch for the smugglers who from the bay and the opposite shore gladly take their course on that side, and on the other side to maintain a watchful eye on the movements of the Jaffna Court, which the Trincomalee servants reported in their secret letter of the 19th of April, recently past, of which by our separate letters of the 1st of May your Esteemed Lordships have received a copy, and of which also our submission of the 4th of June makes mention, the supposed movement of the Kandyan court. Thus we have to your Esteemed Lordships the most dutiful report to make in hope that this closes our Colombo matter as well as that since the aforementioned two Pattamars have been called upon for the general purpose, the esteemed approval of the highest authority will come to bear, the more so since this cruising, as said, yearly, even with the beginning of this monsoon or whenever the same has afforded any opportunity therefor, has taken place.

text_translated_detailed:
Outgoing Letters to Jaffanapatnam
To the Chief Merchant and Dessave [administrator] D. E. Noel Anthonij Lebeck: as Pro-interim commanding officer there. Esteemed, Discreet and Particular Good Friend. You have today had two companies of sipahis march overland from here to there, as mentioned in the enclosed brief strength, whereby is also noted what they have received in wages, etc., and the Manaar servants have been ordered to maintain one company thereof and in its place to send the company of sipahis described with him back here with all speed, and the other to continue marching forward to your location. Upon arrival of the same, you must hold them there and in its place send back here with all haste the strongest company of sipahis from the Manaar, the worthy provided Discreet two at your command, together with the officers belonging thereto, with which after greeting remain /:signed:/ Esteemed, Discreet and Particular Good Friend, your Good Friend /:was signed:/ A. Mooijaart /:in margin:/ Colombo the 8th of July, Year 1765. 

Jaffanapatnam
To the Lord Commander Anthonij Mooijaart
From the Residents at Kilkare, having received word that two Kandyan missionaries disguised in Moorish clothing arrived at Naoer with an inland vessel, this serves as proof that there is poor vigilance; wherefore we insist most strongly on our order by missive of the 10th of this month to cruise diligently and keep a watchful eye on all suspicious foreigners, your Excellency being qualified for that purpose by publication and affixing of bills, promising a premium of 500 rixdollars [modern equivalent: approximately 500 Dutch guilders] to those who apprehend and report such Kandyan missionaries, such that they fall into our hands, with which after greeting remain /:signed:/ Mighty, worthy, Discreet, your Good Friend /:signed:/ Im: will: Falck /:in margin:/ Colombo the 23rd of September, Year 1765. 

To the same as before
Your Excellency is ordered to prevent most strictly the transport of salt to the upper lands

However, we incline toward a contrary opinion, and judge it better to allow the Chiefs who have submitted themselves with them to remain in their posts, because it would not only be hard for these men to see a foreigner placed above their heads, but also the community would unwillingly stand under foreigners. We have therefore already written beforehand to the Esteemed Dessave to allow the old Chiefs to continue provisionally. But since it is a matter of great importance that the inland governance of these new subjects and such orders be arranged as can make our rule agreeable and preferable to them, especially because other korles [korles: similar military/administrative units], observing that they can improve their condition by choosing the Company as their superior, will thereby be encouraged to follow the example of the Kolomna peoples; we have therefore thought it good to request Your Excellency's advice in this matter, concerning the appointment of an Adigaer or Maha Modliaer [Maha Modliaer: a high administrative official] from our old chiefs, and concerning the further means which Your Excellency might judge to be useful in order to make the Company's rule palatable to the new subjects. text_translated_detailed: To as before. Since we have been brought into no small difficulty by the non-arrival of the coolies requested from the Coromandel coast for service in the already begun Expedition, in order to have the necessary baggage and such things belonging to the train carried, this serves to request Your Excellency as principal, with emphasis and very friendly manner, no less earnestly; all Moorish coolie-masters who belong under Your Excellency's command at home, upon receipt of this, to send here, without any exception from them, as having already performed their obligated service for three months' time and to be admitted, since the same must first expire when one has added to each of them 2 rixdollars [rixdollars: modern equivalent: a silver coin] per month and a parra of rice or in place of rice a ropee [ropee: modern equivalent: a monetary unit], which Your Excellency can then also promise them, just as we also expect from Your Excellency's vigilance and zeal for the general welfare of our Lords and Masters; that Your Excellency will manage the household there, despite the absence of the aforementioned servants, or although constrained, nevertheless in such a manner that the work there maintains its progress. We also expect to understand from Your Excellency whether Your Excellency could from the Gale command as well as the Mature Dessavony [Dessavony: an administrative division] still provide us with 500 servants likewise for service in the aforementioned most extremely necessary Expedition; while otherwise the so advantageous and in all respects by the Company made reputable beginnings could be hindered and stopped in their course, as moreover it is known that the maintenance of continual superiority over the Sinhalese nation is nothing but advantageous to us, and the contrary not only brings us disadvantage but is in some cases even irreparable. With which, after greetings, we remain [undersigned] as before [signed] A: Mooijaart, I: I: Feber and D: Burnat [in margin] Colombo, the 20th of July, Anno 1765. To as before. The Head of the Moors of Kaliture, Sekadie Markair Oedoema

text_original: Falck /:in margine:/ Kolombo den 25:' 8ber: A:o 165: Aan als vooren Hierneevens bekomt uE: een Lijst van het getal der koelis in de daar bij vermelde korles, alle onder 't Vaelsch kommandement en de dessavonije van mature geleegen woonachtig: dezelven moeten teegen den 20:e of uitterlijk 25 deeser sonder mancquement hier zijn, dus uw E: op 't nadrukkelijkst gelast word daar over als een zaek van zeer groot belang, sonder interuptie te zorgen, en op, zicht deses de uitschrijvinge 'er van te doen, met deeze bijgevoegde expresse aankundiging dat we hunne betaalinge van 2: rd:s en 1: parra rijst of insteede van rijs 30: stv:s 'smaends niet meer bij partijen maar man voor man zullen laeten volgen, op dat we ons gerust kunnen stellen dat die rechtig geschiede. 'T is bekent genoeg, dat het benoodigde getal uit de Eigentlijke koelis niet zal kunnen gevonden worden, weshalven men de verdere laage geslagten, Jagereros, Tamblinjeros, Raetjes, Porrewettekareassen, enz: te baat zal moeten neemen, onder expresse aankondiging aan de hoofden, dat de omwilligen onder hen, zonder oogluiking, met depontement, en zwaerder, naer bevinding van zaeken, zullen worden gestraft. Bij de Jaalsche koelis moeten een Modliaer en een korael, en bij die van mature twee Modliaers en twee koraels, afkoomen, met de koelis, van Whier verantwoording het wegloopen zal afhangen en zullen ze met den dag van hunne komste alhier worden betaeld Waermede na vrindelijke groete blijve /:onderstont:/ als vooren /:getekent:/ M:s Im: will Falck /:in margine:/ kolombo den 6: december 1765. text_translated_detailed: Falck [in margin] Colombo, the 25th of September, A.D. 1765. To the aforementioned. It is well known enough that the required number cannot be found from the actual coolies, which is why one must make use of the further lower classes, Jagereros, Tamblinjeros, Raetjes, Porrewettekareasses, etc., with express notice to the chiefs that the unwilling among them shall, without any overlooking, be punished with confinement and more severely, as circumstances warrant. text_translated_detailed: Colombo. To the well-born, greatly esteemed Lord Lubbert Jan Baron van Eck, Extraordinary Councillor of the Dutch Indies, Governor and Director of the Island of Ceylon with its dependencies. Esteemed, greatly esteemed, highly commanding Lord. Having just received your well-born, greatly esteemed letter in order that it be transported at the very earliest, I have the honor to perform this most humbly by the bearer hereof. With which, with all due respect and high regard, I remain [under well-born, greatly esteemed, signed] commanding Lord, your well-born, greatly esteemed, most humble and obedient servant [was signed] I: W: Schover [in margin] Manaar, the 29th of December in the year 1764. To the aforementioned. I have the honor to inform your well-born, greatly esteemed most humbly that yesterday over the land route under escort of a sergeant, a corporal, and 12 common Europeans, as well as 20 heads of sipahis and 2 Lascars, 332 pack animals were sent to Putulang, namely 210 pack buffaloes and 122 oxen with 83 beasts of burden or yesterday over the aforementioned animals, namely up to 4 per man, furthermore, although I have also made what effort I could to bring the required number from the others, it has been impossible for me because of the proximity of the wannij [uncertain: wannij], toward which the inhabitants on the other side, at the slightest rumor of being seized and used for some extra service, retreat with all their possessions, claiming to be forced to go there to procure Nelij [uncertain: Nelij] and salt corn, as is now the case, and by such conduct I have been able to obtain more people than the aforementioned 83 men from both this island and the three provinces on the other side. Regarding the aforementioned beasts, I also note most humbly that these, being hired, will come to cost more than by way of purchase, which is why I have taken them over from the owners,

W. Schoren. [in margin] Manaar, the 28th December, Anno 1764. —. By your Well Honored and Esteemed, the reverenced writing of the 12th January has been seen by me with heartfelt sorrow, having observed your Well Honored and Esteemed's displeasure concerning the cross patchiallangs, which, having been brought to the mouth of the river, have lain there in order to be brought over the threshold at the occasion of high water, which on this side gives only at times of full and new [moon] in time over the threshold, in order to carry out the crossing according to your Well Honored and Esteemed's highly esteemed command, which however has not been able to succeed, whatever effort I have also applied to it. Colombo. To the esteemed and respectable gentlemen Anthony Mooijaert and Marten Rein, commander of the Kingdom and Jaffnapatnam and Kandy, as well as presidents and members of the Secret Committee there.

Esteemed and respectable gentlemen,

By means of the enclosed copy of a Kilkare letter dated the 12th of this month, your esteemed gentlemen will come to understand the movements which the followers of the king fled from the court of Kandy are newly beginning to make at the Rameswaram court. Thus I take the liberty to most dutifully communicate the same to you and at the same time to offer a missive received from the aforementioned Kilkare, for which and all other matters this being directed most humbly, I have the honor otherwise to sign this with much respect. Your esteemed gentlemen's commanding lords, your esteemed gentlemen's humble and obedient servant, signed I. W. Schorer. In the margin: Manner, the 17th of May, Anno 1765.

To the aforementioned, the Sipahis [Indian soldiers] consisting of two companies, mentioned in your esteemed gentlemen's respected letters of the 8th of this month, which came overland as well as 28 men who departed from there by inland vessel toward here, have arrived here. Of these we have assigned the company for Jaffnapatnam, and yesterday according to the aforementioned command we undertook the journey overland. Standing ready for tomorrow, the aforementioned 28 men, since there are many sick and weak among them, are to be sent forward by vessel to Jaffnapatnam. And as soon as the remaining 40 men, together with their captain from Costi, have arrived here, we shall have them march forward there. And thus the company that has been stationed here for a long time.

To the aforementioned. It serves solely to give your esteemed gentlemen knowledge in all respect that, after the dispatch of the Sipahis who were here toward Costi under the supervision and oversight of a capable soldier, as a daily master sent to me from Jaffnapatnam, the bearer of this being Corporal Johannes Lijgt van Sterrenbergh, to go along as daily master, as your esteemed gentlemen will come to understand from the enclosed copy of the letter obtained for that purpose. Over which I have, upon the favorable approval of your esteemed gentlemen, left the aforementioned soldier as a language-skilled person with the aforementioned Corps of Sipahis, so that after the delivery of the same men according to your esteemed gentlemen's kind pleasure, he may be sent back here or held at Costi. With which I remain with all high respect and deep respect. Your humble servant, signed J. W. Schover. In the margin: Manner, the 31st of July, Anno 1765.

To the aforementioned. The Sipahis mentioned in your esteemed gentlemen's kind letter of the 29th of July past, consisting of 1 captain, 1 ensign, 2 sergeants, 3 corporals and 33 common soldiers, have arrived here.

To the most noble, greatly esteemed Lord Mr. Jman Willem Falck, Governor and Director of the Island of Ceylon and its dependencies.

Most noble, greatly esteemed, highly commanding Lord,

The Kilkare servants, as evidenced by their letter herewith most humbly enclosed and communicated to us, have reported that some Kandyans in Moorish dress arrived at Nacaur with an inland vessel and subsequently, with the help of the Tanjore prince as well as the Chancellor of the Treasury of the Theuver, sought to seize some war troops in order with the same to land at Pesale and Tallemanaer, as well as the bay of Mudenpattu, Illipe Carre, which is the western shore of the Wanni. Thus we are obliged to give your most noble, greatly esteemed Lord most respectful knowledge of this and most humbly to request that through your most noble, greatly esteemed care we may be assisted with a company of good Sipahis or Malays, since the Sipahis stationed here as well as at Jaffnapatnam are for the most part sick, weak, and impotent, and with the same no least resistance can be made in case of need.

To the aforementioned. With which I remain with all respect and high regard, your most noble, greatly esteemed, highly commanding Lord, your most noble, greatly esteemed humble and obedient servants, signed.

The orders issued by your most noble, greatly esteemed Lord by the highly respected circular letter of the 19th of September just past concerning the patrolling and guarding of the shores hereabouts to prevent and obstruct the passage of war supplies from the mainland to Ceylon were strictly observed here, and likewise care was taken that no foreigners pass over and back without passes. The same I hereby most dutifully and with the required respect give knowledge to your most noble, greatly esteemed Lord. I further note likewise that whatever effort I apply, I cannot however learn how the emissaries of the Kandyan king arrive on the mainland and which way they take there. But according to received letters from Kilkare, through the help of my spies, I have understood that the aforementioned emissaries presented themselves as Jaffnapatnamers, as your most noble, greatly esteemed Lord, if it pleases, will come to understand from the transport letter herewith most humbly accompanying.

Furthermore, I hereby give your most noble, greatly esteemed Lord most respectful knowledge that the patrolling is now being carried out of the Adam's Bridge and Tallemanaer along the north side of this island by the Patchialang, the best dignity and five vessels, together with the western shore of the Wanni as far as Poincorijen, not the Patchialang's the Haasje and oversight, together with a Jaffnapatnam vessel, the undersigned.

text_translated_detailed: Year 1765. From the above-mentioned. The Moor Segoe Abdul Kader mentioned by your Esteemed Excellency in the highly respected missive of the 18th of August last, on the 29th of the last passed month appeared here having shown a certain Moor named Mira Lebbe together with a small boy who with a license letter among other boatmen overland from Kochi [Kochi] came here for departure to the other side with the statement that this one is being sent by the court's great ones there to proceed at Palkoebere [Palkoebere], so I have caused the same to be taken into custody at once in order to send him to Kochi [Kochi] at a suitable and secure opportunity, just as the same shall also under your Esteemed Excellency's gracious approval be transported with the Chialoup [small boat] De Nagelboom, since the bearer hereof, which is sufficiently laden with the Udepittis [uncertain: possibly a type of goods or merchandise] thieves, I have found no secure storage place for the same. While hereby I most humbly submit to the consideration of your Esteemed Excellency the declaration that the aforementioned arrested Moor Mira Lebbe has been granted here together with his license letter brought from there. Therewith furthermore the humble freedom I use to beseech your Esteemed Excellency in God's keeping and remain with all obligatory high regard and deep respect [as noted above] [signed:] I: W: Schover [in margin:] Manaer the 11th of September, Year 1765. To the above-mentioned. The aforementioned Moor in my humble letters dated the 11th of this month in the name of Mira Lebbe I am now sending per the bearer hereof being the Chialoup De Nagelboom over and note furthermore respectfully that the Moor Segoe Abdul Kader whom your Esteemed Excellency has been pleased to send here for the indication of the over and back passing Kandyans for his maintenance and necessary sustenance eight stuivers [modern equivalent: small coins] per day is required, moreover that thereupon for the necessity and upon the strong request made by the same in the meantime and until your Esteemed Excellency shall be pleased to provide me with the necessary order regarding this, I have caused to be advanced to him four stuivers [modern equivalent: small coins] per day, trusting that the same shall be crowned with your Esteemed Excellency's favorable approbation. While otherwise I have the honor to remain with all obligatory high regard and deep respect [as noted above as before signed] I: W: Schorer [in margin:] Manaer the 26th of September, Year 1765. To the above-mentioned. For respectful acknowledgment of the receipt of your Esteemed Excellency's highly respected missive of the 28th of the last passed month of September, this most humbly serves to note dutifully that we shall take the command and oversight of the treasury given thereby to our notice, just as the missive received thereby for Jaffanapatnam [Jaffna] we have at once sent overland as seemed fit to him, moreover the Kilkari letter [letter from the Kilkari/local official] of which your Esteemed Excellency in the aforementioned highly esteemed letters was pleased to mention, upon receipt of the same which was on the 28th of September last, we have also sent overland to Kochi [Kochi], we trust that it has already properly reached its destination, with which the high honor we have to remain with all obligatory high regard and respect [as noted above] Signed I: W: Schorer in margin Manaer the 9th of October, 1765. To the above-mentioned.

text_translated_detailed: September 1765. To as before That which I your Excellency recently concerning the slipping through of Kandyan missionaries have written is hereby confirmed by the enclosed copy of missives and reports. By the last paper it appears at the same time that they over your Excellency's island their way have found and by the letter can your Excellency see that their intention is, the auxiliary troops, which they hope to obtain, at Pesale and Calmanaar as well as the forest of Mudanpatte and Illiepokarre to unload. Your Excellency is therefore by these orders earnestly commanded not only to let good watch be kept there but also for Pesale one of the cruising patrol vessels and one cruising tonij [small patrol boat] to place and the remaining cruising vessels, so long as the monsoon will permit, north of Manner to let cruise on such places as your Excellency shall deem fit, in order to thwart this intention must your Excellency at the same time copy of this letter and the aforementioned two enclosures to Jaffnapatnam send at the speediest, in order to serve as information for the Ministers there. Also your Excellency must conduct a careful investigation whether there are such persons as the report sets forth, with palanquins from the Wanniyah come over, and of that which your Excellency might come to learn thereof, give me careful report. Wherewith I remain with greetings /:understood:/ as before /:signed:/ Im: will: Falck /:in margin:/ Colombo the 2nd of August 1765 To as before The Moor Segoe Abdul Kadis of whom your Excellency these days a report have sent travels now over in order to point out the Kandyan missionaries at their return. text_translated_detailed: To Colombo. To the well-esteemed, greatly honored, highly commanding Lord. Lubbert Jan Baron van Eck, Extraordinary Councillor of the Netherlands Indies, Governor and Director of the Island of Ceylon and its dependencies. Well-esteemed, greatly honored, highly commanding Lord! Since, according to successive reports received from spies from the Colombo-Kule that the dessave [chief administrator] had departed toward Puttalang, and the peoples in the said Corle as well as in Altacolan were being gathered to be transported there as well, I have deemed it proper to bring this respectfully to the knowledge of Your Well-esteemed Greatness and at the same time to present for your disposition a proposition from the Corael of Cattone, who states that, since he has long lived for years in the said Corle, the inhabitants would willingly submit themselves to his command, especially since they all had been unwilling in the war and much preferred to go to Puttalang or elsewhere outside their district to the king against the Company. [I propose] to go down to the Walue and remain there for some time and to occupy the post of Polwatte with 50 sipahis [Indian soldiers]. The lieutenant van den Berg with his detachment [will] again take positions at the Walue to keep an eye on the inland and to remove from them all exceptions which they might otherwise be able to claim. Should this meet with Your Well-esteemed Greatness's approval, I shall apply all my work and vigilance to execute both this and the expedition in the Colombo Corle speedily and carefully. The prize which Your Well-esteemed Greatness sets upon it is so agreeable to me that I remain with high respect [as before] [signed] A: De Lij [in margin] Matara the 8th, Anno 1765, January. To as before. The Corael of Cattone, again summoned, presents difficulties. However, I shall try through W. a small expedition to Cattone to make them disappear. The Lascorins under the Modliaer.

From over Waluwe I have received no adverse news, the Lieutenant van den Bergh being encamped at Meddegamme at the great salt pan, preparing to form a retrenchment or palisade. I have deemed it my duty to inform your Excellency of this and to repeat my request for some malt and medicines for the aforementioned detachment, and under note of the receipt of your Excellency's letter of the 29th of April, I have the honor to be /:undersigned:/ as aforementioned signed:/ A: De Lij /:in margin Mature, the 17th of May, Anno 1765. Colombo. To the aforementioned. After having attempted everything to maintain a correspondence with the Honorable Commander in Kandy through spies and local runners, I have finally received news through the Modeliar of Madoeanwijle in the Colomba Corle, which is related in the Extract herewith. Furthermore, I shall endeavor to obtain some essential information directly from Kandy from the aforementioned Commander, which I trust will be agreeable and meet with your Excellency's approval. I remain with attention /:undersigned:/ as aforementioned. Signed A: De Lij in margin Mature, the 25th of May, Anno 1765. text_translated_detailed: Honorable, High Commanding Lord. I shall have the honor to answer your Well-Esteemed, Most Honorable secret letters of the 14th and 16th shortly. In the meantime, there is being sent under arrest to that place a Sinhalese washerman named Siemcoetie Sajackarege Sikoe, an inhabitant of Dondra, who is suspected of being a Kandyan spy, as your Well-Esteemed, Most Honorable will be pleased to observe in No. 1 and 2, Extracts from the reports of the Commanders at Catoene and Wallalgodde, where he was apprehended. His own voluntary declaration accompanies this likewise under No. 3, from which your Well-Esteemed, Most Honorable will be able to observe how he was captured with Mr. Leembruggen, how matters proceeded with the peoples in the presence of the aforementioned Dessave, and which chiefs were involved therein, likewise an account of what has transpired since his presence with the Adigaer in Kandy, the capture of Kandy, the retreat of our detachments, the present situation of our detachment in Kandy, the fortification of all roads, etc. I would have been satisfied with this declaration, and since it could happen that your Well-Esteemed, Most Honorable would wish to hear or interrogate the person further, I have deemed it best to send him under arrest at your disposal. text_translated_detailed: margin Mature, the 19th of August, 1765. To the aforementioned. In respect to comply with your Well-Esteemed, Most Honorable's desire by secret letter of the 14th and 16th of this current month, I say that the Honorable Captain van Berskij, with whom I have been pleased to maintain good harmony, departed yesterday to Galle, and I further have the honor to present to your Well-Esteemed, Most Honorable herewith a project drawn up by myself and the Honorable Captain Bilfelt with all attention having been devoted to consulting with the aforementioned Captain, the only one of the military gentlemen who possesses local knowledge of the island's situation here, in order to prevent all circumstances that might occur concerning our own subjects and the King's peoples, and we have thus been unable to make any other arrangement than what will appear in the aforementioned list. The same is so arranged that through its execution the islanders can be given nothing but a good impression, and the King's peoples kept in check so as to undertake nothing against the Company's own jurisdiction, the Colomba Corle and over Waluwe, where other matters are understood. To clarify this for your Well-Esteemed, Most Honorable, I shall herewith add as a foundation for everything two Instructions, not of my foreknowledge and by order of the Governor, His Grace, issued by the Honorable Major Medeler to the respective Commanders. Subsequently, I shall proceed to the posts. No posts are being withdrawn except Berlepannetotte, which is unnecessarily occupied as long as Wallalgodde is occupied. Wallalgodde up to 100 men, besides one or two small bands of lascars [lascars: Indian soldiers/sailors], must be maintained at that Corle in the Company's possession in order to secure it for the Honorable Company in case of an accommodation with the Court of Kandy, with foundation, as it formerly belonged to the Honorable Company, and a cinnamon-yielding district. This post is occupied only with Malays on account of its unhealthiness alone, because they endure it better there than Europeans, who here as well as at the Waluwe mostly find their death. The general opinion is that the water of the river flowing by there is the cause of it, at least the people get hardened bellies and constricted chests, which could also result from the salt-like vapors and heavy mists. Wallalgodde has a fine palisade with two pieces of metal cannon of 4 pounds, two small mortars, all with their appurtenances. Catoene is to be garrisoned with 50 Malays, also on account of the unhealthiness and scarcity of livestock and other provisions. These 50 men, as soon as Wallalgodde is attacked, shall march up there for its reinforcement. However, not before a detachment has arrived at Tangale. The old fort of Catoene could well be repaired at the Honorable Company's expense of 2 to 3,000 rixdollars [modern equivalent: rixdollars]. Herewith I have the honor to present to your Well-Esteemed, Most Honorable the plan. I await only the order, or whether the restoration shall be commenced or merely left as is. Tangale is to be strengthened

As an example, when the Captain at Tangale receives news from Catoene that there is trouble, he breaks camp with 200 to 250 men along a fine royal road. His Majesty departs at 7 o'clock and arrives at 3 to 4 o'clock in the afternoon. The rest of the time is calculated on Catoene, and thus with the Waluwe lying between Tangale, Catoene, and Waluwe, they form, so to speak, an equilateral triangle. text_translated_detailed: Here lies a fine palisade of forest wood having interior guard warehouses, etc., which is named by the Dessave [Governor] at its construction a very unhealthy post, just as has already been cited before from Wallalgodde, yet it must nevertheless remain occupied: 1. because all convoys for Berregamme must stop there, at night, namely: 2. to prevent the plundering inhabitants from across the Waluwe from making incursions into the Company's territory, 3. to always serve in case of superior force as a safe retreat for the detachment at Berregamme, and indeed 5. because the crossing over the river Waluwe is thereby protected. Berregamme is a healthy post, a sufficient palisade three hours' journey in Sconings land. This serves to preserve the salt pans up to Magamme for the Company's benefit and to prevent the Kandyan from obtaining knowledge of that. This post is therefore highly necessary and would have been better served with another 50 Malays, but most of the Easterners are either not or are cadavers, so that of the 500, no 200 are capable of doing great damage. Yet the Lieutenant Chattillon has managed everything in flight and has already several times driven off, massacred, and captured such small parties. The said Lieutenant has also offered himself in case of reinforcement with 100 Malays and 50 Lascorins to surprise the temple Cadregam, the sanctuary of the Singhalese, and to plunder it, being from his post 5 miles away, of which here with your Excellency's great and honorable respectful knowledge is given. Acuras is an old Portuguese fort; the same should remain in case one should have to send a detachment to one of the Corles such as Belligam, Gangebadde, and Candebadde, where provisions are in store; 2. one can conduct all commands across the river by thonij [small boat] to there, and if that post should have to be retained by superior force

text_translated_detailed: De Sij [in margin]. Mature, the 10th of September, Anno 1765. To as before. The required Elephants, consisting of four males and two females, are departing today under such escort as the enclosed list dictates. Since moreover some 56 draught oxen have already been purchased and paid for in the Colona Corle and elsewhere, these have also been sent yesterday to Costij according to the enclosed Bill of Lading, while the remaining purchase according to Your Honour's great commands shall be excused, with which advice I take the high honour to sign these with the required high respect. [Understood as before.] Signed. A: De Lij in margin. Mature, the 17th of September, Anno 1765. To as before. Your Honour's Great Respectability, the Circular missives dated the 19th of this month having been well received by us, we cannot refrain from testifying in respectful response thereto that we shall cause the ordered matter to serve us for proper notice and observance, whereby we take the humble liberty to sign this with all desired high respect. [Understood as before.] Signed. A: De Lij I: H: Lappe, L: C: Frobus and P: A: de Moor [in margin]. Mature, the 24th of September, Anno 1765. To as before. Your Honour's Great Respectability, most esteemed letters of the 6th of this month I have had the high honour to receive properly. The order contained therein by Your Honour I shall endeavour to fulfil to the utmost of my ability, exert all my duty, and admonish the heads most earnestly to provide according to the list sent to us as speedily as possible from this Dessavonie and the subordinate Korles and Pattoes the required coolies with specification of how much each head shall have to provide, not without explicit announcement at the same time to those chiefs that the unwilling among them shall without exception be punished with dismissal and severely according to the circumstances of the case. text_original: Mature Aan den E. Arnoldus de Lij opperkoopman en dessave. Eerzame Diskreete. Op het van VE. bij brieve van den 2: deezer gegeven berecht, dat de korael van kattoene zich aengeboden hadde, de kolona korle, waer in lange Jaeren gewoond hadde, en wiens inwoonders zich gaerne aen zijne beveelen, zouden onder worpen, voor d'E. komp: te konquesteeren, mits hij geadsisteert werde met 25 malijers, en permissie erlangde 80. à 100 assurante Inlanderen opte zoeken, tegens de gagie van 3 ropijen 1 ropij en 1. parra rijst of in dies plaets trp 'smaends, hebben wij ten eersten gedelibereert, en beslooten dien voorstel te amplekteeren uE: moet dus gem: korael met 25: fluxe malijers, onder een goed officier van dien landaart ten eersten assisteeren, en tot het uitvoeren van die belofte en het bij een brengen van de noodige inlanders behulpsaam zijn; mitsgaders aan de ingezeetenen van die korle bij olas laeten verzeekeren, dat zij tot de komp: overkomende zich van eene rechtvaerdige Regeering kunnen verzekert houden. Wij hebben, om die diversie van die kant grooter te maeken ook geresolveert de van ginter bij een gebragte Laskorijns voor 't grootst gedeelte, te emploieeren, om onder bevel van den geweezene sabandaer van Belligam Dessanaike modliaea; eene indasie te doen, in 's konings Landen over de waluwe geleegen en zich van de zoutpannen aldaer mitsgaders van de panoasche Dessadonij, en wat daer aen annex is, meester te maeken. Hij keert dus heeden met vierhondert Laskorijns ende bij zich hebbende Porra witti Kariassen te rugge en moet met vijfen twintigh flike malijeas, onder, een bequaem officier van die natie geassisteert worden. text_translated_detailed: Matara. To the Esteemed Arnoldus de Lij, head merchant and dessave [uncertain: administrative official]. Esteemed and Discreet [Sir]. Upon the report given by Your Esteemed [rank] by letter of the 2nd of this month, that the korael [uncertain: possibly a local chief or leader] of Kattone had offered himself, the korle colony, in which he had lived for many years, and whose inhabitants would gladly submit themselves to his commands, to be conquered for the Esteemed Company, provided he were assisted with 25 maliyers [uncertain: possibly a type of soldier or laborer], and obtained permission to recruit 80 to 100 assured inland people, against the wage of 3 ropijen [modern equivalent: a monetary unit], 1 ropijen and 1 parra [uncertain: possibly a unit of measurement] rice or in its place trp [uncertain: abbreviation unclear] monthly, we have at the first opportunity deliberated and resolved to embrace that proposal. Your Esteemed [rank] must therefore assist the aforementioned korael with 25 fluxe maliyers [uncertain: possibly a type of soldier], under a good officer of that nation at the first opportunity, and be helpful in the execution of that promise and the gathering of the necessary inland people; likewise assure the inhabitants of that korle by proclamation that they, coming over to the Company, can be assured of just governance. We have, in order to make the diversion from that quarter greater, also resolved to employ the laskorijns [uncertain: possibly a type of vessel or military unit] brought together from Ginter for the greater part, in order to make an invasion, under the command of the former sabandaer [uncertain: possibly a military rank] of Belligam, Dessanaike modliaea [uncertain: possibly a name], into the lands of the king lying beyond the waluwe [uncertain: possibly a river or boundary], and to make ourselves masters of the salt pans there, as well as of the panoasche [uncertain: possibly a place name] Dessadonij [uncertain: possibly an administrative division], and what is annexed to it. He thus returns today with four hundred laskorijns and bringing with him Porra witti Kariassen [uncertain: possibly a type of vessel or military unit] and must be assisted with twenty-five fluxe maliyers [uncertain: possibly a type of soldier], under a competent officer of that nation. Your Esteemed [rank] will be able to make yourself agreeably useful to us through these enterprises in every possible way, /undersigned/ Esteemed and Discreet, Your Esteemed [rank's] good friend, /was signed/ L. J. van Eck. /in margin/ Colombo, the 5th.

It appears to me not only but also to several Members in the Secret Council that the Militia in Your Excellency's Dessavonia [administrative district] is spread far too thin, to great burden of the Singhalese in the raising of necessities, and that several posts could be withdrawn without harmful consequences, likewise that one post at the Waluwe, one at Kattona, would be sufficient to keep the korles in respect; provided that at Mature a garrison of three hundred men, half European, were maintained, in order, if necessary, at all times to be able to send a respectable detachment into the korles. But since this is a matter of importance, which at the same time requires local knowledge so as not to make a mistake, you must with the commanding captain carefully consider the same, and share with me their common opinion thereon in detail and clothed with reasons. With which I remain with great respect. Honored, Discreet, Your Excellency's good friend. By order of the well-esteemed greatly honored Lord Mr. Iman Willem Falck, Governor and Director of the Island Ceylon with its subordinate territories, was signed J. G. van Angelbeek, secretary, in margin, Colombo, the 14th of August, Year 1765. To as before. Hangakoon must come to the Maha Modliar first. Herewith Your Excellency receives a List of the number of coolies in the districts mentioned therein, all under the Taalsch [Tamil] command and the dessavonij [administrative division] of Mature situated there. These must be here by the 20th or at the latest the 25th of this month without fail, thus Your Excellency is ordered most emphatically to see to this as a matter of very great importance, without interruption, and to oversee the recruitment thereof, with this attached express announcement that we shall no longer allow their payment of 2 rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch silver coins] and 1 parra rice or instead of rice 30 stuivers [modern equivalent: small Dutch coins] per month to be made in batches but man for man, so that we can assure ourselves that this is done correctly. It is well known enough that the required number cannot be found from the actual coolies, wherefore one shall have to make use of the further lower classes, Lagereros, Tamblinjeros, Raatjes, Porrewetchareassenenz [uncertain: local labor classifications], under express announcement to the Chiefs that the unwilling among them, without any overlooking, with deportment and heavier punishment according to the circumstances of the case, shall be punished. With the Taalsch coolies there must come one Modli [uncertain: local official] and one corral [uncertain: local official], and with those of Mature two modliaeas [uncertain: local officials] and two corals, for whose responsibility the running away shall depend, and they shall be paid from the day of their arrival

text_translated_detailed: Gentlemen. Having arrived here yesterday newly from the Command of Jafnapatnam, there have come 84 Coppen Camatjes consisting of 7 sergeants, 5 tandel and 72 common soldiers, so we have not wished to detain them here any longer, but have today, under the supervision of 1 corporal and 2 common soldiers, together with 1 Cangaan and 4 Lascorijns, sent them on to Chilauw, having provided them with rations as far as Costi, and we have further the honor to subscribe ourselves with the utmost humility, as Your Esteemed Excellencies' obedient and humble servants. [Signed:] I. Thornton, I. Brasch, and J. J. Sweedberg. [In margin:] Calpettij, the 18th of August, 1765. Yesterday evening at half past six I received from Chilauw a letter from Your Esteemed Excellency addressed to Captain Bodenschats, accompanied by a copy of a letter written by Your Esteemed Excellency to the commanders of Nigombo and from them to those of Chilauw, as well as one from the last-mentioned commander directed to me, dated the 30th of the past month, noting that the said Captain Bodenschats had lain that night with three vessels on the Chilauw roadstead and would undoubtedly be in need of fresh water and firewood when he might arrive with his fleet under this headland. I have therefore today in the morning subscribed myself with all humility, as Your Esteemed Excellencies' obedient and humble servant. [Signed:] T. Thornton. [In margin:] Year 1765. — Calpettij, the 22nd of May. Colombo. Having arrived here yesterday newly from the Command of Jafnapatnam, there have come 84 Coppen Camatjes consisting of 7 sergeants, 5 tandel and 72 common soldiers, so we have not wished to detain them here any longer, but have today, under the supervision of 1 corporal and 2 common soldiers, together with 1 Cangaan and 4 Lascorijns, sent them on to Chilauw, having provided them with rations as far as Costi, and we have further the honor to subscribe ourselves with the utmost humility, as Your Esteemed Excellencies' obedient and humble servants. I. Thornton, I. Brasch, and J. J. Sweedberg. Calpettij, the 18th of August, 1765. Yesterday evening at half past six I received from Chilauw a letter from Your Esteemed Excellency addressed to Captain Bodenschats, accompanied by a copy of a letter written by Your Esteemed Excellency to the commanders of Nigombo and from them to those of Chilauw, as well as one from the last-mentioned commander directed to me, dated the 30th of the past month, noting that the said Captain Bodenschats had lain that night with three vessels on the Chilauw roadstead and would undoubtedly be in need of fresh water and firewood when he might arrive with his fleet under this headland. text_translated_detailed: Khalpettij [uncertain: possibly a place name or administrative term]. To the Chief, the Junior Merchant Thomas Thornton. Good friend. In answer to your letter of the 22nd current, it is noted that the recovered Lieutenant Scheerken is to be approved to come here at the earliest opportunity, while this is directed solely to that end, so I remain with great [respect] [understood:] Good friend, your good friend. By order of the well-esteemed, greatly honored Lord Governor van Eck [signed:] J.s Reintous, sworn clerk [in margin:] Colombo, the 27th of March, Year 1765. To as before. This being directed solely as an escort to the enclosed bill of lading of the cargo loaded in the bringer of this, with which also travel the Military Captain Francis Albertus Prins, Ensign Bernhard Isaak de Bellon, and 51 soldiers, to whom your excellency must arrange proper transport to Putulang, so we remain with great [respect] [understood:] as before. By order of the esteemed members of the secret council [signed:] I.s Reintous, sworn clerk [in margin:] Colombo, the 17th of April, 1765. To as before. The shortage of coir rope [karwaat: a type of rope made from coconut fiber] is great, therefore we order your excellency to send us as much of it as soon as possible, as much as you can obtain on hand or in a day or three. With which, with great [respect], I remain [understood:] as before [signed:] By order &c. I. G. van Angelbeek, secretary [in margin:] Colombo, the 7th of November, 1765. To as before. I approve what your excellency has done to obtain a letter to be handed to Captain Bodenschats, and because the coir rope had not yet passed, I doubt whether it will be of good success. Under humble submission, I further offer a translation of a report made by the Arraatje Mutu regarding his actions at the Rammenadewaram Court, or properly at the Albashik [chief minister] of the same, Jammadrumpulle, to whom he brought no other message than that my order regarding the aforementioned Kandyan Prince would be answered. Thus I at the same time took the opportunity at the proper time to respond to the request that he Jammoderumpulle had made to Kilkare to demand from me for the cost 2 rolls of red, one roll of blue, and one roll of green velvet, as well as two rolls of damask, possibly on the assumption that one and another would be a gift for the freedom obtained of the aforementioned Kandyan Prince.

text_translated_detailed: To as before. The wandering envoy of the dethroned Candianese king, who according to the matter dealt with previously had proceeded to the Sickelse Naik, having there had some gold works made, proceeded therewith on the 5th of this month in company with the aforementioned Sickelse Naik to make an offering to the Albeschik of the Maruas Kingdom Jammoderumpulle, who upon receipt of this sacrifice had allowed himself to be moved to detain this Envoy in order, against a recompense of 30,000 rixdollars [modern equivalent: a substantial sum of currency], of which one half was to be given before and the other after the troops would be ready, 8 to 10,000 warkarras [uncertain: local currency or goods] for a payment of 4 pagodas [modern equivalent: Indian gold coins] each month and a month's wages to be provided to him, promising under the counter-gift of a palanquin to consider this matter further, meanwhile writing an ola [official letter/decree] to the Jansjoursen prince without it being known until now what the contents thereof are, although there is also the rumor that from Jansjaaur some vessels would come to Tewiepatnam for the removal and transport of these peoples according to information received from Kilkare, of which the first resident Keunneman has thus been seriously instructed by me to inform himself further in the most secure manner, and if so, to protest most vigorously with Jammoderumpulle against all such enterprises against the Company and furthermore to give immediate notice to Your Well-Born Esteemed Sir and the Madras ministry of the foregoing and whatever else he may learn concerning this, and through the cruisers at hand stationed in the Pantjalling, the Friendship and three armed thonijs [small vessels], in particular to keep watch against the aforementioned crossing, but also considering this number necessary to be increased and strengthened, of which to give first notice so that he may be met from here as much as possible, under which humble communication I take the liberty with deep reverence

The delicate circumstances at Kilkare concerning the far-reaching audacious undertaking of the Albeschik of the Rammenadewaram Court Jammoderumpulle, in particular regarding the collection of monies which the recently departed Candianese Prince promised to him and for which the resident Keunman had interposed himself, I find myself obliged to show to Your Well-Born Esteemed Sir most respectfully, with the enclosed four copies of letters from the aforementioned resident and the appropriate answers thereto, accompanied by a copy of a concept protest ola sent by me to Rammenadewaram, all of which I trust will merit Your Well-Born Esteemed Sir's favorable approval. And since truly the garrison here is weakly and poorly stationed, having only 39 effective common soldiers in service, owing to the smaller number than the regulation stipulation of 12 heads, and Kilkare for the manning of the cruisers requires more manpower, besides which one of the recently arrived has already died and three more lie in the Hospital, and moreover many of the others also look poorly both on account of swelling and otherwise, I venture most humbly to renew the petition made by submission letter of the 4th of September last, for assistance of soldiers to such a number and provision as Your Well-Born Esteemed Sir in his high wisdom shall see fit

Esteemed Commanding Lord! I have the Teero Your Excellency with the most due respect to inform of the receipt of Your Excellency's very honored secret [letter] of the 9th of this month, and furthermore that on the 12th thereof a certain emissary from Rammenade Supermania Modeli warane came to me in the name of Jammodrum Pulle without any ceremony, claiming on behalf of the matter of the Prince conveyed to Kolambo by obligation and promise 8700 pagodas. I had informed myself before his coming regarding the emissary and the execution from Candia come PalKomoedeaar, and of which Your Excellency's commanding will hereafter have the honor of doing a proper report, so I answered this emissary that I had well understood his request, and moreover that I was just busy writing an ola [a letter or decree] to Tammoetaram bulle in which this Chancellor would have provided for everything that was necessary, and moreover that this would also at the same time serve as an answer to this made request. This emissary thereupon asking whether I would pay that money, I answered him that Lammoetarampulle could obtain this from the ola to be sent to him by me, with which this emissary then departed very discontent. On the 13th thereof my arraatse [a messenger or official] would go to Bammenade waram with an ola, of which the concept is herewith enclosed in all respect, with the hope that its contents may be favorably approved by Your Excellency. My arraatje now coming with this ola to kammenadewaram, Jammoetarampulle did not wish to accept it and read it, although the arraetse of his own motion presented it several times in two days and merely fruitlessly urged its acceptance until the Chancellor gave order that the arraatje should no longer come within and to him

Clercq To As before In continuation of the respectfully submitted letter enclosed herewith from myself and the merchant and Colombo's First Warehouse Masters, the Honorable Pieter Liebert Schmidt, I have the honor to report to Your Noble and Esteemed Lordship that the Honorable Valiant Captain Bodenschatz appeared on shore the day before yesterday, making known that he had received only the first letter to come this way and to remain in readiness for further orders. Thus, having immediately turned his course hither, the second order to proceed directly from where he found himself to Castle [Castij] to the freshwater island, as the first [order] was sent, could not be delivered to Monsieur through the intermediary to His Excellency, but was shortly after his arrival there sent back from there. The aforementioned Captain Bodenschatz has also made known that while His Excellency on the 13th of this month, as he lay at anchor at Kilkare, had gone ashore, the Resident Keunman received news that the Young Cheuver [local ruler] lay very ill at the Maselan, of which, however, no direct communication has yet appeared. Yesterday evening late I had the honor to receive over Manaar [Mannar] and Kilkare Your Noble and Esteemed Lordship's venerated letters of the 24th November last, and since the snow the Postillion was dispatched yesterday regarding the delivery of the ammunition and goods from the sloop Princess Isabella or otherwise as it still lies at anchor, I take the liberty to inform Your Noble and Esteemed Lordship hereby most respectfully that firstly to Jassanapatnam [Jaffnapatnam] and Manaar [Mannar] the changed circumstances at Kilkare have been communicated, so that vessels and goods of the Cheuver, having been seized, may be released and therewith not be sailed away with. text_translated_detailed:
Tuticorin [Tutticorin:] To the Honorable Gerrit de Vos, merchant and chief [opperhoofd: chief official/head]

Honorable, Discreet [Sir]

We are sending the small ship De Batavier [The Batavian] to you, so that it may be forwarded to Kilkare [Kilkari/Kilkari], in order to fetch from there and bring back to us the Prince, regarding whom you will see our intention in a separate letter to the Resident Keunemans dated the 21st of April last, which letter is transmitted to you under flying seal for speculation. And although we believe that the instructions we have given to Keunemans regarding this matter will be sufficient, we nevertheless qualify you to add further dispositions in case any unknown circumstances should require them, such that they serve to achieve our objective in this matter. We also leave it to you, as being closer at hand, to judge whether Keunemans can be spared for so long as to conduct the aforementioned Prince back here, with which we remain with great respect, [signed] Honorable, Discreet [Sir], your good friends [signed: A. Mooijaart, J. J. Feber, D. Burnat, J. and A. Moens] [in margin:] Colombo, the 31st of May, anno 1765 [below:] P.S. Upon the reports received with the ship Westerveld [Westerveld: ship name] of the attack made by those of Rammanadeswaram [Rammanadawaram: a place in South India] against our lodge and warehouses at Kilkare [Kilkari] that was threatened, we have at once decided to send a detachment of approximately 250 men under the command of Captain Bodenschatz to Kilkare, in order to defend the Company's lodge, servants, and effects, and if those of Rammanadeswaram should proceed to any hostile acts, to repel force with force. We are entrusting the direction of this to you by means of this letter; a copy of our letter and the instruction for the aforementioned Bodenschatz goes to you herewith, whereby for further elucidation we further note that, if the Rammanadeswaram state, which appears to have created this commotion in order to obtain satisfaction for two obligations amounting to 8,700 pagodas [Pagooden: a monetary unit], which the Resident Keunemans granted without authorization, should continue to urge payment of the same, you must declare firmly that the Company will never pay them, since Keunemans never had authorization, order, or power to pass obligations in the Company's name, and the Company cannot be held responsible for the bad actions of subordinate residents.

Honorable, Discreet and Particular Good Friends

Upon the news brought here by a Coromandel merchant vessel that the lodge at Kilkare had been set on fire and abandoned, we have immediately dispatched orders to Jaffnapatnam [Jaffanapatnam: a VOC settlement] and Mannaar [Manaar: a VOC settlement] to have the strait of Pambe [Pambe: a waterway] and the coasts of the Seuver [Sjeuverheers: a region], territory, most closely occupied and patrolled, and to detain and take into custody all vessels, subjects, and goods of the Seuver, for our indemnification in due time. Although we do not doubt that such naturally occurring means of reprisal will already have been set in motion on your part, we nevertheless qualify you for this, in addition, and to set in motion further such factual and gentle means for obtaining speedy satisfaction as you, being closer at hand, can better judge than we to be the most useful and appropriate. For this the command of Captain Bodenschatz, who sailed yesterday from Negombo [Nigombo: a VOC settlement], will be of service to you. We expect prompt communication of the success of these measures, and if an unexpected and sufficient satisfaction should follow, you must also give notice of this to Mannaar and Jaffnapatnam, so that the arrested vessels and goods are not held longer than necessary. We remain with great respect [signed] as before [signed:] Iman will Falck, I. J. Feber, I. G. van Angelbeek, and A. Moens [in margin:] Colombo, the 24th of September, 1765. To the chief on the coast of Madure, The Esteemed Discreet P:r [Patron] of the Johanna Catharina and the Patjallang, freedom. The letter from the Kilkare Resident Keuneman, dated the 23rd of September, I received only on the 7th of this month, after I had already received yours of the 26th of September ten days before, with a copy of Keuneman's letter. To my astonishment, the translation of the Malabar letter, which the envoys of the Sikkels Naik and of Palkoem had arranged with such great care to be delivered to the Governor of Colombo, contained nothing other than a private consultation of the said Palkoem elder to his brother-in-law, who has come with ours from Kandy, to do his best to bring about an agreement between us and the prince of Kandy. Since therefore the letter itself, although it was addressed to me, belonged to the said Moor, I have not been able to understand until now what the messengers intended with their mysterious message, much less that any answer on my part was required. You must make this known to Keuneman and send him along with the translation of that Malabar letter, so that he may have the opportunity to speak with the envoys, should they come asking for an answer, and from them possibly to hear how matters stand with the negotiations with the Kandyan king on the other coast, and what His Majesty further intends—whether to make peace or to continue the war.

Doch dat uE: niet te min aen mij van die boodschap, wegens het groot belang van de komp: hadde kennis gegeeven en daar op ordre van mij ontvangen, zijne Excellentie te laeten andwoorden: Dat de Edele kompanie met den koning van kandia in openbaeren oorlog verwikkeld was, en dus uit hoofde der verbonden en onderlinge vriendschap van Hem vertrouwde, dat hij de zendelingen van dien koning of zijnen aanhang geen gehoor en geene hoope van de minste assistentie zoude geeven, alzo zulx zoude weezen eene inbreuk der subsisteerende alliance en vriendschap die de kompe naer haere merite zoude moeten opneemen, also alle de geenen, die den koning van kandia in deezen oorlog min of meer adsisteerden daar door tvonden, vijanden van onze komp: te zijn, dat ik dus zijne Excellentie niet alleen liet verzoeken, om die zendelingen ten eersten van zijn hof te doen vertrekken, maar ook uit hoofde van de onderlinge vriendschap, ons te onderrechten,
text_translated_detailed: Kilkare. To the Bookkeeper and First Resident Hendrik Willem August Keuneman. Good friend. Regarding the message from Tommoderam Pulle, that the father-in-law of the Kandyan king has requested from him 5,000 men of auxiliary troops against the E. [East India] Company, you must answer him at the earliest opportunity in the most appropriate manner. That it seems strange to you that His Excellency can entertain the slightest objection to what he ought to do in that case, since he surely knows that, by virtue of the treaties of long standing between the Noble Company and the Rammanadewaramsche [Rameswaram], which subsist for the maintenance of close friendship and alliance, such a request must be rejected without the least hesitation. That you also hold yourself assured that he has never been in doubt as to which side he ought to choose in this matter, since His Excellency has always shown himself to be a friend of the Company. We have received your secret and separate letter of 6 April last and the four olas mentioned therein from that person who presented himself to you as a legitimate Kandyan Prince. The olas are dated 19 March previously, which we note in order to learn from you why these were not forwarded earlier than the 6th of the following month of April. From their contents it appears that this personage is not a Kandyan Prince but a Malabar nayak [regional ruler] and of the same family as the king of Kandy whom we have driven out, and that the relationship which he can have to the Kandyan throne is at most based on affinity by marriage. Since we are nonetheless extremely interested in getting to know him closely and being thoroughly informed about everything concerning him and his descent, you must inquire carefully into all matters, and particularly also to what extent he is related to the two last kings of Kandy, as well as regarding his personal qualities and manner of living. Please give us a detailed report on this.

text_translated_detailed: the departed superior, the head merchant Mister Rein, concerning the reported landing of eight Englishmen on this Island, the departure of seven of them, and the stay of one at Kandia [Kandy], to which your Excellency, with the subsequently received discrepant reports, has been pleased to insist with emphasis in order to discover whether there is anything to it or not, his Excellency has nevertheless been unable to learn anything up to now, the rumors of which beginning to be silent—to say nothing more—nevertheless the inquiries shall continue, and the same have been likewise recommended by reiteration to the Batticaloa head, D.E. Pfeijffer, recently. Meanwhile, we trust that your Excellency will be most graciously pleased to qualify us, as soon as the Monsoon will permit, to withdraw a good portion of the garrison at the Vendeloose Bay [Trincomalee area] again in order to have as many men continue to garrison there as the circumstances shall require, for although the First Undersigned would well wish to be able to make use of that garrison to carry out the named project at Jamenkarwij [Jaffna region] mentioned by the departed superior, the weakened garrison here will not permit this to be attempted for now, considering that sickness and death in the encampments and especially at Samblegam [Jaffna] continue to spread. The sick coming from the encampments are being replaced, and they must moreover still be reinforced beyond the garrison itself, which would require quite another arrangement should English ships appear here. Therefore, we trust that your Excellency will be pleased to consider this. Besides, the reoccupation of Jamenkarwij [Jaffna region] is a matter of the province which the Company can proceed with when it pleases, and which the First Undersigned undertakes to carry out when the opportunity presents itself most favorably.

To the aforementioned. We have the honor to communicate most respectfully to Your Excellency with great respect that the Tamenkarwijse chiefs, upon the written invitation of the undersigned to come over again to the Company's side, have through intermediaries in response made known that they were not at all voluntary but rather were forced by the superior power of the Kandyans to choose their old side again. That upon their first submission a promise had been made to them to station a detachment for their protection in their province, but since this had not happened, the Kandyans, as one might think, had molested them and forced them to the rechoosing of their side; and finally that they are now again not unwilling to go over to the Company if one would only be willing to protect them against all hostile attempts of the Kandyans by sending a detachment into their province to take post there. But since this is indeed their genuine sentiment and one has not been able to do so before and is even less capable at present, however reasonable their request also is, since our weakened garrison cannot undertake the same, we shall keep those entirely not unwilling clients in good humor for the time being and satisfy them with promises, in the hope that Your Excellency with great respect, considering this most favorably, will be pleased to assist us with some military reinforcement so that we can fulfill the aforementioned request. We therefore humbly request that for the reason that the possession of the Tamenkarwijse lands is not only advantageous for the Company but the inhabitants indeed from time to time show signs of their good disposition, with which we have the honor to subscribe ourselves with the deepest veneration and high regard. Rfeijffer, in his letter to the Company's common letter of today's date regarding the request for permission of discharge are consistent with the truth, so there come to obtain that headship, should the same become vacant, from here two supplicants, namely the under-merchant and Administrator D. text_translated_detailed: of the Island of Ceylon with its dependencies. Most Esteemed and Highly Honored Sir. As reluctantly as my predecessor as well as I have wished to come before Your Most Esteemed and Highly Honored Sir with complaints regarding the increasingly troublesome behavior of the Wannia [regional chief] of Kattekolompattoe and Jamblegam Sanderesegere Nelle Maxane, it has nevertheless proven unavoidably necessary that this has already occurred more than once, as I hereby take the opportunity through this repeated complaint to renew my grievances, considering that this man merely appears to embrace the Company's protection in outward show and secretly maintains no small correspondence with the enemies, particularly with the fallen Wannias of Pattaij, Madewaetje, and Natoe, the last of whom is married to his daughter, to whom he not only shares what passes through the Company's territories but also furnishes him salt and other lacking necessities, and moreover has entirely ceased to concern himself with fulfilling his repeated promises and obligations under the contract made with him, or to show any obedience whatsoever, as evidenced by irrefutable proofs supplied these days: First, that in violation of what was promised by contract to lend the Majors a helping hand in collecting head taxes from the subjects residing in his provinces, he has not only directly refused to do so but has treated the Majors with contempt, notwithstanding that he allowed this in the first years and brought nothing whatsoever against it. Second, that when I ordered him to contribute to the salt tax in fulfillment of his contract due to the shortage of salt, he has likewise absolutely refused to do so. Third, that he completely blocks the passage of certain descendants who wish to come here to bring their goods or to bring certain provisions, preventing them from being able to proceed further on their way here.

text_translated_detailed: Trincomalee. To Captain Commandant Lodewijk von Frijtag. Together with the Secret Council. Manhafte Vroome. In answer to your Excellency's two secret missives of the 14th and 20th of December last, it serves with regard to the first that Tamerkarwij should be reoccupied as soon as the monsoon permits and the vessel can sail back and forth, provided that Vendeloos Bay is not too greatly depleted of people in that time, and upon occupation the detachments from there, likewise from Vendeloos Bay and Koetjaar, being sufficiently positioned in a triangle, at least not far from one another, can at all times sail back and forth, if not reconnoiter, at least correspond daily with one another. text_translated_detailed: Coolies or Camoetjes [uncertain: possibly referring to laborers/porters] have been summoned from Pondicherry, of which we receive word daily. In the margin: Nagapatnam, in the castle on the 18th of May, 17[65]. Not before the 29th of the past month of June was I handed your Excellency's letter, namely from the 1st of the same month, together with copies of your Excellency's letters directed to their High Excellencies, the Esteemed High Government, although my intention was not to impose such trouble upon your Excellency, I am nonetheless obliged to you for it, as through this I have obtained a detailed and complete report of the past glorious military campaign and the present state of affairs. It has not pleased Heaven to allow the Esteemed Lord van Eck to reap the fruits of his glory and to bring to execution the other well-reasoned propositions that have been presented to their High Excellencies, which in my judgment would principally consist of the destruction of the royal authority, which would be beneficial for the Company and would put an end to further otherwise to be feared wars. But since your Excellency, before the receipt of these letters, to my astonishment remained long in transit from their High Excellencies' intention and disposition regarding this matter, you will already have been informed, I shall not elaborate further on this. Your Excellency I now assure that the correspondence shall be maintained and that your Excellency shall receive from here all possible assistance, just as then for the sake of the required coolies, seeing that from Pondicherry towards there, the Esteemed van Tijlingen told me that he had written for that people, no word came. I sent new people, who reported to me that because the French were busy rebuilding Pondicherry and Carrical, the coolies there could find abundant work and were not disposed to come over. Yet upon a further sending and offer of greater payment, already six hundred, as I am informed, have agreed to come and are expected daily. The vessels for their transport are in readiness, so I do not wait impatiently for their arrival. I am promised that the still lacking four hundred and possibly even more—for I have requested up to 2,000—will also be arranged. However, one cannot rely on this, for this people are much given to speaking and promising but slow and poor in execution. Regarding the person Moettoe Soepper Narresinga Maharasa, such a person is not known here, at least not under that name, and therefore it appears that the aforementioned person has only recently assumed that name, as is customary when such people attain some dignity or strive for it. text_translated_detailed: In the margin: Nagapatnam, the 17th of August 1765. To the aforementioned. The Ceylonese ministry having requested that we send them 1000 to 2000 coolies [laborers], of which 676 heads were already sent in the month of July last past, now 14 days ago another 73 were sent, and now 120 more are going, of which 43 heads belong to the first batch sent and have already been charged to our cost account, and the remaining 77 are from a later recruitment, since no more could be obtained. We shall now subsequently send the entire accounting with the same, and there shall also go over three persons who present themselves as overseers of them, but in reality are soul sellers [recruiters] who still seek to profit something from their wages. The head over a hundred heads earns 7 pagodas [Indian currency], 2 Mandoors [overseers] at the aforementioned rate 3½ pagodas each, and common men two pagodas. It runs somewhat high in cost, yet I have preferred to agree to somewhat more rather than to delay the Expedition. For two months they have received payment in hand until the 23rd of October, and the agreement is that their wages must be paid to them monthly and that after the expiration of six months they have the freedom to leave the service. I am with all respect [signature mark] as aforementioned. Signed J: Haksteen. In the margin: Nagapatnam, the 25th of August in the year 1765. text_translated_detailed: Coromandel [Coromandel Coast] To the Noble Lord Christiaen van Tijlingen, Governor and Director over the Company's important trade and commerce on the said Coast, Residing at Nagapatnam. text_translated_detailed:
To Jan Feber and Jan P. van Angelbeek [in margin:] Colombo, the 10th of July 1765:

Our European military force has suffered so greatly through the nearly continuous marching back and forth that we are compelled to have more than one hundred men from the Colombo garrison, who have become unfit for service partly through wounds, partly through weakness and chronic illnesses, sent back to Europe, besides those who have chosen to be sent to Batavia, or whom we must distribute here and there in places where the service is easier; and besides a considerable number who are unfit at the detachments in the field and in the remaining garrisons outside Colombo, through sickness and disease, and cannot be used for any command. Since, moreover, the four ships that have arrived have brought scarcely 500 healthy soldiers instead of the promised 800, we find ourselves greatly hindered in being able to fill the positions of the fallen, wounded, and unfit, at some very weakened companies, and we are therefore compelled to seek assistance from your Excellency. If we could only be supported with one hundred common soldiers from the Coromandel garrisons, we would see ourselves relieved from our predicament for the time being, and we bind ourselves to repay your Excellency's assistance with double the number at the slightest change of affairs for the better (which God grant). As before. As before. We also send your Excellency by Lieutenant Letanche a model cartridge pouch, which we request be made as soon as possible in the quantity needed and sent back here with the return of the aforementioned commandant, with which we remain with respectful greetings and esteem. [signed below:] as before [signed:] Im. will. Falck, Jan J. and Jan P. van Angelbeek [in margin:] Colombo, the 10th of July 1765:

Our European military force has suffered greatly through the continuous marching back and forth, so that we are compelled to have from the Colombo garrison more than one hundred men, who have become partly through wounds, through weakness and chronic illnesses, unfit for service, to have [them] repatriated, besides those who have chosen to be sent to Batavia, or whom we must distribute here and there in places where the service is easier; and besides a considerable number who are unfit at the detachments in the field and in the remaining garrisons outside Colombo, through sickness and disease, and cannot be used for any command. Since, moreover, the four ships that have arrived, instead of the promised 800, have scarcely brought 500 healthy soldiers, we find ourselves greatly hindered in being able to fill the positions of the fallen, wounded, and unfit at some very weakened companies, and we are therefore compelled to seek assistance from your Excellency.
